paper_diagnosis: Pulmonary manifestation of Plasmodium falciparum malaria: case patient 1
disease_label_per_paper: P. falciparum malaria presenting with acute ARDS and shock physiology
presentation_summary: 29-year-old man presented after 5 days of fever, flu-like illness, cough, and shortness of breath after earlier outpatient antibiotics for presumed upper respiratory infection.
Chest radiograph and CT showed bilateral diffuse alveolar infiltrates and ground-glass opacities consistent with ARDS.
On arrival he had respiratory distress, pulse 125/min, blood pressure 80/60 mmHg, respiratory rate 30/min, temperature 39.0 C, and room-air oxygen saturation 80%.
ABG showed pH 7.33, PaO2 52.9 mmHg, PaCO2 50 mmHg, HCO3 26 mEq/L, and PaO2/FiO2 ratio 106; echocardiography showed normal LV function.
Initial labs showed thrombocytopenia, mild AKI, hypoalbuminemia, hyperbilirubinemia, transaminitis, high LDH/CK, and CRP 318 mg/L.
Urgent blood smear identified P. falciparum ring forms with parasitemia 1.3%; he received IV artesunate and intensive respiratory support.
